mcq.question: Why does `find_free_bed()` return a `Bed*` rather than a `Bed&`?

options.A: A pointer can be `nullptr` to say 'no free bed'; a reference must always refer to an object
options.B: References cannot be returned from member functions
options.D: A reference would copy the bed

mcq.explanation: A reference has to be bound to a real object, so it cannot express 'nothing found'. A pointer can, but the caller must check it before dereferencing.

mcq.question: A pointer to the first element of a `std::vector` is stored, then `push_back` is called on that vector. What can happen to the stored pointer?

options.B: It may dangle, because the vector may have reallocated its elements to new storage
options.C: It is automatically updated to the new address

mcq.explanation: When a vector's capacity is exceeded it allocates a larger buffer and moves its elements there. Every pointer, reference and iterator into the old buffer is invalidated.
